solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: New American president lacking inspiration

indicators.note: something new is a fresh version, so these letters are made over into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A newly elected US president is dismissed as uninspiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like it describes the president, but it is the anagram signal working on A plus PRESIDENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian writing or ideas are dull and prosaic, lacking any spark of imagination.

clue.text: Picked up light bucket

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: pale means light in colour

explanation.surface: Someone picks up a light bucket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' looks like lifting the bucket; it signals the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A pail is a bucket, typically for carrying water or milk.

clue.text: Knock over ornament

definitions.meaning: to knock them to the floor
to ... is to adorn, as in ... the halls

explanation.surface: Someone knocks a decorative ornament over.
explanation.definitionFit: Deck is slang for punching someone down and also means decorate or adorn.

clue.text: Coordinated cooking cosy hot dinners

indicators.note: cooking the letters means mixing them up into something new

parts.note: H is an abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Warm, comforting dinners all cooked at the same time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' sits naturally beside dinners as kitchen talk, but it is the anagram signal; 'hot' gives just H.
explanation.definitionFit: Synchronised actions happen at the same moment, carefully coordinated in timing.

clue.text: Counters in section of bistro terrace rotated

indicators.note: rotated says the hidden letters are read backwards
a section of the phrase bistro terrace holds the letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Counters set out in part of a restaurant's terrace, turned round.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Counters in section' as the definition; 'in section of' is the hidden-word indicator, so the definition is just 'Counters'. 'rotated' reverses STROTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To counter a remark is to reply sharply, so retorts are verbal counters.

clue.text: Goaded some bears no end, withholding last of salmon

indicators.note: bears means carries, so the first word holds the next inside it

parts.note: any can mean some, as in 'have you any?'

indicators.note: withholding means the letter is kept back, removed from the word
the last letter of salmon is the one taken

explanation.surface: Bears are endlessly provoked when denied their salmon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bears' looks like the animals but is the verb 'carries': ANY holds NO. 'withholding' takes N out of END.
explanation.definitionFit: Being goaded means being provoked or needled, which leaves one annoyed.

clue.text: To some extent, antidepressant brought about change

indicators.note: brought about, like a ship turning, says the run of letters is read backwards
only part of the word antidepressant is used, so a run of its letters is taken

explanation.surface: Taking an antidepressant has partly changed someone's outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To some extent' takes TIDE from inside antidepressant; 'brought about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to alter or revise it, so it is a verb for making a change.

clue.text: Sad a cake Nigella initially promoted is ruined

parts.note: feeling down means feeling sad

indicators.note: promoted means raised higher, so in this down clue the letter moves up the word

parts.note: a donut is a ring cake

indicators.note: the initial letter of Nigella is the one moved

explanation.surface: A sad cake that Nigella Lawson promoted turns out to be a failure.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigella Lawson is a British TV cook. 'promoted' lifts the N of DONUT to its front, making NDOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone down and out is destitute, financially ruined and without resources.

clue.text: Yeti's drool spoiled child's figurine

indicators.note: spoiled means messed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A child's toy yeti is ruined by its own slobber.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy soldier is a small model of a soldier, a classic plaything for children.

clue.text: Volatile criminal caught in very short time

indicators.note: the criminal is caught, held inside the word for a moment

parts.note: an instant is a very brief moment
a con is a convict, a criminal

explanation.surface: A volatile crook is arrested in no time at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inconstant is changeable and unreliable, as a volatile temperament is.

clue.text: Rock and roll's influence

definitions.meaning: to move to and fro, rocking and rolling
... is power or control over others, as in holding ...

explanation.surface: A comment on the cultural impact of rock and roll music.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Rock and roll' as the music genre; here it means the swinging motion.
explanation.definitionFit: Swaying is a rocking motion, and sway also names authority or influence over people.

clue.text: Heard lamenting nip from grey parrot climbing plant

indicators.note: heard means the word is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: mourning means grieving, lamenting

indicators.note: a nip, a small bite, is the first letter of grey

parts.note: a lory is a small brightly coloured parrot

explanation.surface: A lamenting grey parrot gives someone a nip.
explanation.definitionFit: Morning glory is a twining vine whose trumpet flowers open early in the day.

clue.text: Small fruit in middle of pharynx — tracheotomy ordered

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put into a new sequence
the central letter of the word pharynx is the one taken

explanation.surface: A small fruit has lodged in a patient's throat, and a tracheotomy is ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' sounds medical, but it rearranges R (the middle of pharynx) with TRACHEOTOMY.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherry tomato is a small variety of tomato, botanically a fruit.

clue.text: Type of book that's left lying to one side?

definitions.text: Type of book that's left lying to one side?

parts.words: Type of book that's left lying to one side?
parts.note: this kind of book sets lies, invented stories, aside and deals only in fact

explanation.surface: A book abandoned on its side somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying' reads as resting flat, but means telling untruths: fiction is lying, and this genre leaves it aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Factual writing such as history or biography is the opposite of invented stories.

clue.text: EC provider wasted too much?

indicators.note: wasted means wrecked, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A European service provider is accused of charging too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overpriced costs more than it is worth, an excessive charge.

clue.text: Patent element of odometer, instrument clipped inside vehicle

indicators.note: one element, the first letter, of the word odometer is taken
inside places the shortened instrument within the vehicle

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle

indicators.note: clipped means the instrument loses its last letter

parts.note: a viol is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A patent for a component of a car's mileage gauge, fitted inside the vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patent' suggests an invention but is the adjective meaning plain to see. 'clipped' drops the instrument's final L.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent as an adjective means evident or plain, the same as obvious.

clue.text: Bare earth, muddier at intervals by delta

parts.note: an earth is a fox's den

indicators.note: every other letter of muddier is picked out

parts.note: Delta is D in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Muddy, bare ground beside a river delta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bare earth' reads as one phrase, but 'earth' is a fox's DEN. 'at intervals' takes UDE from muddier.
explanation.definitionFit: Denuded land is stripped of its covering, left bare.

clue.text: Heavy metal from Iron Maiden covering Queen, mixing it up at first

indicators.note: covering means the iron and maiden letters wrap around what follows

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
R, for Regina, is an abbreviation for queen

indicators.note: the opening letters of the words mixing, it and up are taken

explanation.surface: The band Iron Maiden cover a song by Queen and give it their own twist.
explanation.walkthrough: Iron Maiden and Queen are rock bands, a fitting picture for 'heavy metal', but here 'Maiden' is a cricket over with no runs and Queen is R for Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Fermium is a heavy radioactive element, a synthetic metal named after Enrico Fermi.

clue.text: Two cents jamming cheap old plaything

indicators.note: jamming means wedged in, so the cents go inside

parts.note: mean means stingy, cheap
C is an abbreviation for cent, so two cents give CC

explanation.surface: A cheapskate offers two cents for an old toy.
explanation.walkthrough: Meccano is a model construction kit of metal strips, nuts and bolts.
explanation.definitionFit: Meccano is a construction toy, so a child's plaything.

clue.text: Doctor to nurse: "Close shave!"

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor tells a nurse about a narrow escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a person speaking; it is the verb that rearranges TO NURSE. 'Close shave' usually means a near miss.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsure is the shaved crown of a monk's head, quite literally a close shave.

clue.text: Something given up for good?

parts.note: the item is surrendered in part exchange for a new purchase, goods, not forever

explanation.walkthrough: 'for good' reads as permanently, but the item is handed over in return for a new good.
explanation.definitionFit: An old car or phone handed to a dealer as part payment for a newer one.

clue.text: Almost trap ten coppers in former place of business

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, losing its final letter

parts.note: to corner someone is to trap them
X is the Roman numeral for ten
coppers are low-value coins, small change

explanation.surface: Police nearly trap a gang in an old commercial building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police; here it is loose coins. A corn exchange was a building where grain merchants traded, many now converted.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn exchanges were halls where grain was bought and sold, a trading venue of the past.

clue.text: Even bits of woodland taken up to make trench

indicators.note: taken up in a down clue means the letters are read upward, backwards
the even-numbered letters of woodland are picked out

explanation.surface: Scraps of woodland are dug up to make a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even bits of' takes ODAD; 'taken up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: In woodworking a dado is a groove cut across a board, a narrow trench.

clue.text: Strip, posing naked

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its outer covering, here the first and last letters

parts.note: to pose a question is to ask it, so posing means asking

explanation.surface: A striptease, posing in the nude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'posing naked' sounds like modelling; 'posing' is ASKING, and 'naked' strips off its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To skin something is to strip off its outer layer.

clue.text: Creep among penguin chicks

indicators.note: the answer sits among the letters of the words penguin chicks

explanation.surface: Something creeps in among the baby penguins.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch forward is to move slowly by small degrees, to creep.

clue.text: Child, when beginning to kick, faced with appropriate rebuke

indicators.note: faced with puts the appropriate word in front, facing the others

parts.note: to appropriate something is to take it
a tot is a small child
as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'

indicators.note: only the beginning, the first letter, of kick is used

explanation.surface: A child starting to kick out gets a suitable telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' reads as the adjective 'suitable' but is the verb meaning take.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone to task is to scold or reprimand them, an idiom for rebuke.

clue.text: Central point of European lecturer, looking back

indicators.note: looking back says the combined letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: A European academic reflects on the main point of an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A node is a junction or focal point where lines or branches meet.

clue.text: Reading perhaps when Riley and Dent finally come in for day of Countdown

indicators.note: the new letters come in, replacing the letter standing for day

parts.note: taken as written, the name of the TV quiz
D is an abbreviation for day

indicators.note: the final letters of the names Riley and Dent are taken

explanation.surface: Countdown's Rachel Riley and Susie Dent step in for a day.
explanation.walkthrough: Countdown is a British TV word-and-numbers quiz, with Rachel Riley and Susie Dent among its presenters. Reading is the county town of Berkshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading is the administrative centre of Berkshire, an example of a county's chief town.
